newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sets out Chechnya recovery proposals.
newsitem.headline: Russia sets out Chechnya recovery proposals.

text.p: Russia has sent detailed proposals to the self-declared government of Chechnya to assist recovery in the war-torn region ahead of elections called for late January, a senior Kremlin official said on Friday.
Ekho Moskvy radio quoted Ivan Rybkin, secretary of the powerful Security Council, as saying that the proposals covered political, economic and social questions.
He said the documents would be considered at a meeting on Sunday chaired by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and by the Security Council the following day.
Rybkin said the proposals set out "by days and weeks" the steps to be taken up to January 27, when the separatists have called parliamentary and presidential elections.

The 21-month Chechen war was halted in August after Rybkin's predecessor, Alexander Lebed, later sacked by President Boris Yeltsin, signed a peace deal with the rebel leadership following a flare-up in fighting.

Chernomyrdin, keen to play a more active role in the region, plans to visit Chechnya in the near future and may hold talks with the separatist leaders. Last month he signed a detailed accord in Moscow with rebel leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev setting a framework for economic cooperation between the two sides.
The new Russian proposals include political plans on the kind of temporary agreements and protocols needed until the elections, Rybkin was quoted as saying.

Rybkin's deputy, Boris Berezovsky, continued his tour of the Causcasus on Friday and held talks in Tbilisi with Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze. He said agreement in Chechnya had to take into account the desires of all parties, including Russia, Chechnya and Georgia.
